stickseum/getting-started.b:
:: Characters = 25
:: Classic modes = 6
:: Minigames = 8
:: Players = 2–32
:: Platform = Browser (no install)
:: HP = 300

Stickseum is a real-time stickman brawler. It opens right in your browser with nothing to install, and one link is all it takes to get friends into the same room. There are 25 characters, 6 classic modes, 8 minigames and 10 daily modes, and anywhere from 2 to 32 players can play together.

## How to open the game
- Hit **Play Now** on the site and the latest version opens right away.
- If you'd rather have a file, download it and double-click it. You still need an internet connection, though.
- When playing with friends, everyone should join through **Play Now**. If versions differ, chat, skins or new characters may not show up for some people. If someone joins on a different version from the host, a notice pops up in the room.
- Change the language in Settings. You can pick Auto, Korean, English, Español, Français, Deutsch or 日本語.

## Your first steps
1. Pick a nickname (up to 12 characters).
2. Choose a mode in **Online Play** and start matchmaking, or create a room in **Private Play** and send the 6-character code to your friends. Codes use uppercase letters and numbers.
3. Pick your character when the match starts. You get 15 seconds to choose, and once everyone has picked, all choices are revealed for 3 seconds.
4. Want to get a feel for things first? Practice solo in **Practice Mode**.
5. New accounts can play a 7-step tutorial. Finish it and you get 100 gold.

## Matchmaking and bots
- Online matchmaking puts people looking for the same mode into the same room. You don't pick the map; it follows a rotation that changes every 10 minutes.
- If the room still isn't full 15 seconds after the last person joins, bots fill the empty slots and the match starts. Rooms of 16 slots or fewer get filled completely; bigger rooms get filled up to 10 players.
- Bots can't play Hide and Seek, so that mode waits until enough real players join. Bots never join Ranked either.
- In private rooms, the host adds bots manually. Bot difficulty can be Easy, Normal or Hard.

## Basic rules
- Every character has 300 HP (except in modes that set their own HP).
- When you die, you usually respawn after 5 seconds. Some modes change the respawn time or don't let you respawn at all.
- There's no natural regeneration. Instead, if you stay in the same spot for 3 seconds, you heal 5 HP every 0.5 seconds. Standing still and shooting is fine. Survival and One Shot have no healing.
- Teammates can't pick the same character (except on large maps where teams are so big that duplicates are unavoidable).
- In Duel, you can't pick a character you already used in an earlier round.

## Controls at a glance (defaults)
- A / D to move, W or Space to jump, aim with the mouse and click to attack.
- Q is Dash, E is Teleport, R is Ultimate, F is Skill. See the Controls & Settings page for the full details.

## Base cooldowns
- Skill 5 seconds, Ultimate 20 seconds, Teleport 10 seconds.
- Dash is 1.5 seconds by default (0.7 seconds for Assassin).
- Teleport isn't instant: it charges for 1 second before moving you.

## Saving your progress
- If you're not logged in, gold, skins and levels are saved only in the browser you're using. If the site address changes or you open the game as a file, you start fresh.
- Log in with a Frenchfries777 account and your progress (gold, cosmetics, level, mastery, achievements, missions, Season Pass and more) is also saved to your account. Log in on another device and it will load or merge your progress. When merging, whichever side has more progress wins.
- Friends, clans, Ranked, parties and gifts require you to be logged in.

## Good to know
- If the game tab goes into the background, the browser slows it down and it may look frozen. Keep the tab in front while you play.
- Practice Mode and private rooms don't give rewards like gold, XP, achievements or missions.
- The site help recommends a computer since it's a keyboard-and-mouse game. That said, touch controls turn on automatically on touch devices.

stickseum/controls-settings.b:
:: Move = A / D
:: Jump = W or Space
:: Dash / Teleport = Q / E
:: Ultimate / Skill = R / F
:: Emote wheel = V (up to 8)
:: Frame Limit = Unlimited / 60 / 30 FPS

Here's everything about keyboard/mouse and touch controls, plus what you can change in the Settings screen.

## Keyboard & mouse (defaults)
- A / D: Move left/right (the tutorial says you can use the arrow keys too)
- W or Space: Jump
- Mouse: Aim, Click: Attack
- Q: Dash, E: Teleport, R: Ultimate, F: Skill
- Enter: Chat, V: Emote wheel, Tab: Scoreboard (shown while held)
- S or Down arrow: Used to fly down as Dracula in bat form, and to move into the darkness below as Kurus while in darkness.
- The bat (Baseball Player) doesn't hit with just a click. You have to swing: hold the click, pull the mouse down, then bring it back up.
- Teleport (E) moves you to where your mouse is pointing. It charges for 1 second after you use it, then moves you.

## How ability keys work
Skill, Ultimate, Dash and Teleport keys behave according to the **Ability Activation** setting. The default is the first option.
- **Hold and release to use**: An aim indicator appears while you hold the key, and the ability fires when you release. Click while holding to use it at that spot.
- **Press to use instantly**: The ability fires the moment you press the key.
- **Press once to aim → press again to use**: The first press aims, the second press fires.
- In any mode, Esc or right-click cancels aiming. Clicking while an ability key is held doesn't count as an attack.
- Hold Shift and press the Skill or Ultimate key to use it right away on the nearest enemy. A mint-colored circle briefly appears over that enemy.

## Rebinding keys
- In Settings under **Key Bindings**, you can change Move Left, Move Right, Jump, Dash, Teleport, Ultimate, Skill, Open Chat and Emote — 9 actions in total.
- Click the slot you want to change, then press the new key. Press Esc to cancel.
- Each key does only one thing. If you pick a key that's already in use, the action that had it gets your old key instead.
- Esc, Tab, Space, the arrow keys and S can't be used as the chat key.
- **Reset to Defaults** puts everything back. On-screen help text updates to match your new keys too.

## Quality-of-life settings
- **Sound Effects**: On or Off
- **Screen Shake**: On or Off
- **Graphics Effects (skin effects, etc.)**: Auto, High, Medium, Low. Auto adjusts based on game speed. If the game stutters, try lowering it.
- **Control Type (Mobile / Computer)**: Auto-detect, Mobile (touch), Computer (keyboard & mouse)
- **Frame Limit**: Unlimited, 60 FPS, 30 FPS
- **Show FPS**: On or Off
- **Ability Activation**: The three options described above
- **Show Damage Numbers**: On or Off
- Settings are saved in this browser.

## iPad & phones (touch)
- Touch controls turn on automatically on touch devices. Devices with a mouse or trackpad connected are treated as computers. If your iPad has a keyboard/trackpad attached, try switching to Mobile manually in Settings.
- Move with the left joystick. Push it up to jump, push it down for a down input.
- Pressing the red joystick on the right attacks, and you aim in the direction you drag. If an enemy is near the aim direction, the aim snaps to it, and a short tap on the aim side attacks the nearest enemy.
- Buttons: skill, ultimate, jump and 💨 (dash and teleport). Tap 💨 to dash and hold it to teleport; the teleport goes in the aim direction. The emote button (😀) is at the top right.
- The Ultimate and Skill buttons auto-aim at the nearest enemy.
- The joystick appears where you put your thumb, and the buttons are small and transparent so they block less of the screen.
- The ⛶ button in the top right toggles fullscreen.
- If you hold the device upright, you'll be asked to rotate to landscape.

## Emotes & chat
- Press V to open the emote wheel. The 8 default emotes are 👍 😂 😡 😭 🔥 👋 ❓ 💀. You can add or remove emotes bought in the shop, and the wheel holds up to 8.
- Press Enter to open chat and Enter again to send. Esc closes it.
- After using an emote, you can use another one after 1.2 seconds.

## When you die
- While waiting to respawn, use the arrow keys or your Move Left/Right keys to cycle through living players' views.
- If you're eliminated in Battle Royale, Battle Royale Duo or Tournament, the defeat screen appears right away. Choose **Leave** to exit the room or **Spectate** to keep watching.

stickseum/modes.b:
:: Classic modes = 6
:: Minigames = 8
:: Daily modes = 10
:: Deathmatch = 3 min, most kills wins
:: Domination = Hold the point, first to 100
:: Ranked = 1v1 Duel (best of 3)

Stickseum has 6 classic modes, 8 minigames, 10 daily modes that rotate each day, plus Ranked. The online mode list shows Ranked, Daily Mode, the 6 classic modes, Minigames, then Co-op (Boss Raid and Tournament), in that order. Detailed rules for minigames and daily modes are on the Minigames & Daily Modes page.

## Quick overview
- Deathmatch: Most kills in 3 minutes wins.
- Battle Royale: No respawns, last one standing.
- Battle Royale Duo: Teams of 2, at least 8 players.
- Team Battle: Two teams; wipe out the other team to win.
- Duel: 1v1, best 2 out of 3.
- Domination: Hold the point and reach 100 first.

## Classic modes
- **Deathmatch**: The basic mode, a free-for-all with respawns at the map's default player count (4 on 4-player maps, 6 on 6-player maps, 8 on 8-player maps). Matches last 3 minutes, and whoever has the most kills when time runs out wins. If kills are tied, it ends as a shared win (draw).
- **Battle Royale**: The map's default player count, no respawns. Fight until only 1 is left. When you're eliminated, you can leave or spectate from the defeat screen.
- **Battle Royale Duo**: Teams of 2 fight until one team is left. At least 8 players, and only on 8+ player maps. A team is out only when both members are down. In a party, only 2-person parties can join.
- **Team Battle**: The map's default player count plus 2, split into two teams (6 on 4-player maps, 8 on 6-player maps, 10 on 8-player maps). Wipe out the other team to win.
- **Duel**: A one-on-one, best 2 out of 3 rounds. You pick a new character every round. Characters you've already used can't be picked again, so you'll need to handle several characters to win.
- **Domination**: Two teams fight over the point in the middle of the map (the floating platform closest to the map's center). Holding the point earns 1 point per second, and the first team to 100 points wins. You respawn 5 seconds after dying. Player count is 6–12 depending on the map (6 on 4-player maps, 8 on 6-player maps, 10 on 8-player maps, 12 on large maps). Minimum 6 players.

## Minimum players and maps by mode
- Battle Royale Duo needs at least 8 players, so it only opens on 8+ player maps.
- Domination needs at least 6 players and opens on 4+ player maps.
- Zombie Game needs at least 7 players, so it opens on 8-player maps.
- Survival, Boss Raid and Tournament only open on 8+ player maps.
- Hide and Seek is locked to a single 32-player map (Mega Arena).
- Capture the Flag is played on 4 dedicated large maps, and Parkour on 4 dedicated maps.
- Parkour, Capture the Flag and Mega Arena maps only show up in those modes or in private rooms. More on maps in the Map Guide page.

## Ranked
- A 1v1 Duel (best 2 out of 3) only between logged-in players. No bots.
- Details on points and tiers are on the Ranked & Seasons page.

## Practice Mode
- Pick a map, a character and opponents (None, Dummy, Moving Dummy, Bot) and practice solo. You can have up to 8 opponents.
- Cooldowns are short (Ultimate 3 seconds, Skill 2 seconds, Teleport 2 seconds), and you respawn 2 seconds after dying.
- Capture the Flag and Parkour maps can't be chosen as practice maps.
- No XP, gold, achievements or mastery are earned.

## Private rooms
- The host chooses the mode, map and weapon rules. Classic modes, minigames and daily modes are all available.
- Weapon rules are **Normal Mode** (pick from every character) and **Random Weapon Mode** (each player is offered 3 random characters to choose from).
- Turn on **Auto Team Balance** to even out team sizes. Turn on **Map Vote** to let players vote on the map before the match.
- Private rooms give no rewards like XP, gold, soul stones, missions or achievements.
- If the host leaves or disconnects mid-match, the match keeps going and someone else becomes host.

## After the match
- When a match ends, an MVP vote opens. You can't vote for yourself, and the MVP gets 50 XP. In a match with only one human (for example, playing with bots), the bots vote too and the votes decide the MVP.
- After a match, kill moments are automatically saved as highlights. You can rewatch them on the records screen.

stickseum/minigames.b:
:: Minigames = 8
:: Daily modes = 10 (one per day)
:: Zombie HP = 900
:: Hide and Seek = 1 min 30 s
:: Boss Raid = 4 players · 3-min time limit
:: Tournament = 16 players (1v1)

These are the special-rule modes outside the classics. Here are the 8 minigames and the 10 daily modes, one of which opens each day.

## Zombie Game
- At least 7 players. After everyone picks a weapon, one player is chosen as the zombie (dark green).
- Humans can only damage zombies, and zombies can only damage humans.
- Humans killed by a zombie become zombies. Zombies that die respawn as zombies after 5 seconds.
- If the humans survive for 2 minutes, the humans win. If everyone becomes a zombie, only the original zombie wins (players who turned don't share the win).
- Zombies get 1.45x move speed, 900 HP and 6x attack power, plus faster attacks and a shorter Dash cooldown (half). After resting just 1.5 seconds they heal 10 every 0.5 seconds, and they take no knockback.
- As a human, the basic idea is to avoid fighting zombies head-on and keep your distance.

## Bomb Pass
- At least 4 players. Everyone starts right away as a bare-handed stickman with no weapon, Ultimate or Teleport — only Dash.
- One player starts holding the bomb, and it explodes after 20 seconds. Click a nearby player to pass the bomb (they have to be close to where you're aiming).
- When it explodes, whoever is holding it is out. If more than half of the starting players are still alive, the next round starts after 3 seconds.
- If the bomb explodes once survivors are down to half or fewer, the remaining survivors win.

## Hide and Seek
- At least 5 players, always on the 32-player large map (Mega Arena). Everyone has 1 HP and no Dash, Ultimate, Teleport or weapon choice.
- One player is the seeker, and everyone else turns into a stationary platform to hide. The seeker's screen is covered for 10 seconds, and during that time hiders can move freely to find a spot.
- When the countdown ends, the seeker gets a pistol. A platform hit by the first shot turns back into a stickman (and can move again), and a second hit eliminates them.
- If the seeker finds everyone within 1 minute 30 seconds, the seeker wins; if even one hider is left, the survivors win.
- Bots can't play this mode, so it waits until enough real players join.

## Parkour
- Played on one of 4 dedicated Parkour maps. No weapons, characters, HP, Dash or Teleport — just you.
- The first person to touch the golden platform at the top wins.
- Grab items placed along the platforms to shove nearby opponents out of the way. Items respawn 9 seconds after being picked up.
- The maps are Clear Morning, Above the Clouds, Lava Spire and Starlight Stairs, and up to 20 players can race together.

## Survival
- Only opens on 8+ player maps. At least 6 players, with no weapon choice, Teleport or characters (Dash is available).
- You have 1 HP, so getting hit by a disaster even once means you're out.
- After a 9-second wait, one random disaster hits for 12 seconds: lightning, tsunami, volcano, acid rain, flood, meteors, bombs or zombies. Survive it and it fades, then another 9-second wait begins.
- As rounds go on, disasters come more often, cover more area and move faster. Survive 5 disasters to win.
- If you die early, you can spectate or leave.

## Capture the Flag
- Played on 4 dedicated large maps (Canyon Fortress, Volcano Basin, Sky Fortress, Desert Ruins). Maps hold up to 12 players.
- Two teams (Blue and Red) score 1 point by grabbing the flag from the enemy base and bringing it back to their own base. Your own flag has to be at your base for the score to count.
- The flag carrier moves a bit slower (0.85x) and can't Teleport.
- If the flag carrier dies, the flag drops and returns to its base after 10 seconds. If a teammate touches it, it returns immediately.
- The first team to 3 points, or the team with more points after 8 minutes, wins. If it's tied, the next capture wins.
- You respawn at your base 5 seconds after dying. At least 4 players, and bots can be added in private rooms.
- Capturing a flag gives 50 player XP and 25 character XP.

## Boss Raid
- Only opens on 8+ player maps. Exactly 4 players team up in a co-op mode to take down one giant boss.
- The time limit is 3 minutes. Defeat the boss in time to succeed; if time runs out or everyone is wiped out, you fail.
- The boss is randomly one of Flame Giant, Ice Golem or Thunder Demon King. Its HP is 1500 plus 880 per player. Each boss has its own weapon: the Flame Giant uses a flamethrower, the Ice Golem a piercing ice spear, and the Thunder Demon King bouncing electric orbs.
- The boss slams the ground regularly. When a red circle flashes, jump! Each hit does 22 damage.
- When the boss's HP drops below 70%, 50% and 30%, it moves to the next phase. Phase 1 brings 2 minions, phase 2 brings 2 minions plus floor beams, and in phase 3 the boss goes into a rage and attacks faster alongside 3 minions.
- The minions appear as the Flame Swordsman, Ice Swordsman and Lightning Swordsman to match the boss, and they use the boss's color. They have 150 HP, and there can be up to 5 at a time.
- Team lives are shared: player count times 3, plus 3 (15 for 4 players). Anyone who goes down respawns after 6 seconds.
- On success, you get role bonuses. Damage Dealer (most damage dealt), Tank (most damage taken) and Cleanup (most minions killed) get 25 gold each, and MVP gets 50 gold. If one player earns several roles, the rewards stack.

## Tournament
- 16 players compete in 1v1 best-of-3 matches (first to 2 wins) through the Round of 16, quarterfinals, semifinals and final. Played on 8+ player maps.
- Matches in the same round run at the same time, and you only see your own. Each round lasts 75 seconds.
- You pick a new character every round. Unlike Duel, you can pick characters you've already used.
- Players who are done can spectate other matches. In the final, the arena gradually shrinks.
- Winning earns you titles: 1 win gets Tournament Champion, 5 wins gets Tournament Emperor, and 10 wins gets Tournament Legend.

## Daily modes (special modes)
- One of the 10 modes below opens as the daily mode each day. Today's mode is set by the date and doesn't change for the day.
- In private rooms, you can pick any of the 10 freely.
- **Protect the King**: Two teams, each with one King (crown overhead). The first team to take down the enemy King wins. Non-Kings respawn after 5 seconds. After 5 minutes, the team whose King has more HP left wins.
- **King of the Hill**: Free-for-all. Holding the point alone gives 1 point per second; if two or more are on it, scoring pauses. The point moves to a different platform every 20 seconds. First to 60 points, or the highest score after 6 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Weapon Relay**: Everyone gets the same lineup of 10 characters in the same order. Each kill switches you to the next character, and getting a kill with the 10th character wins. After 6 minutes, whoever is furthest ahead wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.
- **Freeze Tag**: Two teams. When you die you freeze in place, and a teammate who touches you for 1.4 seconds frees you with 60% HP. Freeze the whole enemy team to win; after 4 minutes, the team with fewer frozen players wins.
- **Treasure Raid**: Gold coins keep appearing all over the map. When you die, you drop half your coins and anyone can pick them up. Whoever has the most coins after 4 minutes wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Weapon Roulette**: Every 12 seconds, everyone's character changes at random (cooldowns reset too). Most kills in 5 minutes wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.
- **One Shot**: Everyone has 1 HP. One hit takes you down, and you respawn after 3 seconds. First to 100 kills wins, or the most kills after 4 minutes.
- **Paint War**: Two teams. Stepping on a platform paints it your team's color. The more tiles you've painted, the faster your score goes up; first to 150 points, or the higher score after 4 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Bounty Hunt**: Each kill is 1 point. The score leader (3+ points) gets a bounty (red marker). Taking down the bounty target is worth 4 points. First to 20 points, or the highest score after 5 minutes, wins. Respawn after 4 seconds.
- **Low-Gravity Brawl**: A brawl with weak gravity and strong knockback. You fly high and get launched far. Most kills in 4 minutes wins. Respawn after 3 seconds.

stickseum/maps.b:
:: Total maps = 23 (22 regular · 1 large)
:: Parkour maps = 4 (up to 20 players)
:: Capture the Flag maps = 4 (12 players)
:: Large map = Mega Arena (32 players)
:: Map order = Shuffled in 10-minute blocks

There are 23 maps in total (22 regular and 1 large), plus 4 Parkour-only maps and 4 Capture the Flag-only maps. The player count next to each map name is the default for Deathmatch and Battle Royale. Team Battle adds 2 more players on top of that.

## How maps are chosen
- In online matchmaking, you don't pick the map. The map order is shuffled the same way in 10-minute blocks so people searching at the same time end up in the same room, and rooms are found in that order.
- In private rooms, the host picks the map. With Map Vote on, it's decided by vote before the match.
- In Practice Mode, you can pick any map except the Parkour and Capture the Flag maps.
- Which maps each mode can use is listed under minimum players on the Modes page.

## 4-player maps (width 2200, height 900)
- Grassland, Volcano, Desert, Pyramid. They share the same layout — a flat floor with platforms stacked 5 levels high — and only differ in color and look.
- No gimmicks.

## 6-player maps
- Space, Palace, Cyber, Sky (width 1000, height 1400): Narrow, tall tower layouts. Platforms go up 9 levels, so there's a lot of fighting up and down.
- Steampunk (width 2500, height 1000): Has 2 moving platforms that slide back and forth.

## 8-player maps
- Ocean, Programming, School, Playground (width 2600, height 1000): Wide maps with 3 levels of platforms.
- Sky Station (width 2600, height 1000): Has 1 platform in the middle that moves side to side.
- Colosseum (width 2400, height 900): The center rises in steps.
- Elevator Tower (width 1300, height 1500): A tall map with 1 moving platform.

## 8-player maps with gimmicks
- **Storm Pirate Ship** (2600 x 1000): All the deck platforms sway side to side together. Every 16 seconds a wave sweeps across the floor, and if you're standing on the floor you get pushed up. A dark ripple shows up just before it hits, and the wave alternates direction.
- **Pipe Factory** (2400 x 1000): Conveyor platforms keep pushing anyone standing on them. 4 steam vents take turns blasting; a puff of white smoke appears briefly before each blast, and while it's blasting you get launched high into the air.
- **Underground Mine** (2600 x 1000): A minecart rolls back and forth on the floor rails. Getting hit deals 50 damage and big knockback. Every 22 seconds there's a blackout that darkens the screen, and you can only see inside the lamplight around you and your teammates.
- **Frozen Lake** (2400 x 1000): The floor is slippery, so you slide even when you try to stop. On a 16-second cycle, the middle of the floor cracks (at 9 seconds) and breaks (from 11 seconds), and freezing water shoots up. Touching the freezing water deals 25 damage and bounces you upward.
- **Dark Swamp** (2400 x 1000): There are stair-step platforms on both sides, 3 steps each, and 1 platform in the middle. A large swamp sits in the center; everyone inside it has their move speed reduced by 33% and their surrounding vision limited. Stepping-stone platforms are placed over the swamp.
- **Dungeon** (2400 x 1000): Two groups of iron-bar platforms take turns appearing and disappearing every 4 seconds. They flash red 1.2 seconds before vanishing as a warning.

## Large map
- **Mega Arena** (3000 x 1200, 32 players): The Hide and Seek map. It can also be picked in private rooms. It doesn't appear in regular online matchmaking.

## Parkour maps (up to 20 players)
- Clear Morning (1150 x 2100), Above the Clouds (1300 x 2150), Lava Spire (1050 x 2050), Starlight Stairs (1250 x 2450).
- Every jump on these maps has been checked to make sure it's actually reachable. The golden platform at the top is the goal.

## Capture the Flag maps (12 players)
- Canyon Fortress (4400 x 1500), Volcano Basin (4800 x 1600), Sky Fortress (4000 x 1900), Desert Ruins (5200 x 1400).
- Long, horizontally symmetric maps with a base at each end.

## Map tips
- On narrow tower maps (6-player maps), explosive weapons and high-knockback weapons have the edge. Falling off costs you a lot.
- On wide maps, long-range characters can keep their distance more easily.
- On gimmick maps, try turning the gimmicks against your enemies. Minecarts, freezing water and steam vents pair well with weapons that push opponents.

stickseum/ranked.b:
:: Format = 1v1 Duel (best of 3)
:: Starting points = 1000
:: Rating system = Elo (max 32 per match)
:: Season = 1st of month (Korean time)
:: Top tier = Grandmaster (1550)
:: Leaderboard = Top 50

Ranked is a mode where logged-in players face off 1v1 for rating points. A new season starts every month.

## Rules
- It's a 1v1 Duel, best 2 out of 3. You pick a new character every round, and you can't pick a character you used in an earlier round.
- You only meet other logged-in players. Bots never join.
- Ranked runs in separate rooms, so you only meet people who are also looking for Ranked.
- If both players aren't logged in, the match is played as a practice match and points don't change.
- You can't play Ranked while in a party.

## Points
- Everyone starts at 1000 points at the start of a season.
- Points change using the Elo system. You go up when you win and down when you lose, and the higher your opponent's points compared to yours, the more you gain for winning. The most you can gain in one match is 32 points, and a win always gives at least 1 point.
- The loser's points never drop below 0.
- Between the same two players, only 3 matches within 24 hours change points. Play more than that and the results show, but points stay the same.
- Points only change on the server. The player who opened the match (the host) reports the result.

## Point examples
- Beat someone with a similar score and you gain about 16 points.
- Beat someone 200 points above you and you gain about 24 points.
- Beat someone 200 points below you and you gain about 8 points.
- The loser drops by as much as the winner gains. So high-rated players lose a lot when they lose to lower-rated opponents.

## Tiers
- Bronze: from 0 points
- Silver: from 950 points
- Gold: from 1050 points
- Platinum: from 1150 points
- Diamond: from 1250 points
- Master: from 1400 points
- Grandmaster: from 1550 points

## Titles
- The first time you reach Gold, Diamond or Master, you get a permanent title. The titles are Ranked Gold, Ranked Diamond and Ranked Master. They don't go away when the season ends.
- Pick one from the Title button on your profile to equip it, and it shows above your character's head.

## Seasons and leaderboards
- Seasons last one month and run on Korean time. On the 1st of every month, everyone resets to 1000 points.
- On the Ranked screen, you can see the top 50 players of the current season. Your own points, tier, rank, wins and losses, and win rate are shown too.
- The Leaderboard page on the site also shows this month's Ranked season standings and the clan rankings.

## Don't mix these up
- Ranked tiers (Bronze to Grandmaster, based on points) and character ranks (Novice to Grandmaster, based on kills with that character) are different things. The names are similar, but they go up separately.
- The Season Pass season is one month based on your device's calendar. It runs separately from the Ranked season.
- Ranked isn't a private room, so XP, gold, mastery and mission progress all build up as usual.

## Ranked tips
- Since you pick a new character each round and can't reuse one, it pays to be comfortable with two or three characters.
- You can see what your opponent picked and choose a counter for the next round. You have 15 seconds to pick a character.
- Points don't change after 3 matches with the same opponent in 24 hours, so even if you're winning, it's not efficient to keep playing the same person.

stickseum/characters.b:
:: Characters = 25
:: HP = 300
:: Skill cooldown = 5 s
:: Ultimate cooldown = 20 s
:: Dash cooldown = 1.5 s (Assassin 0.7 s)
:: Teleport cooldown = 10 s

There are 25 characters. Each has a different weapon, Skill (F) and Ultimate (R). Every character shares the same cooldowns: 5 seconds for Skill and 20 seconds for Ultimate. Numbers come from the game's v238 code and the character codex. Detailed write-ups for each character are split across the Guns & Ranged, Melee, Throwing & Explosive, and Shotgun, Cards & Special pages.

## What every character has in common
- 300 HP. That's in the standard modes.
- Each character has a basic attack (click), one Skill (F, 5-second cooldown) and one Ultimate (R, 20-second cooldown).
- Dash (Q) and Teleport (E) are the same for everyone. Dash can be used every 1.5 seconds by default, Teleport every 10 seconds. Only Assassin has a 0.7-second Dash.
- Teleport charges for 1 second after you use it, then moves you. Flag carriers can't Teleport.
- While stunned, you can't move, attack, Dash, Teleport, or use your Skill or Ultimate. Samurai can't be stunned during their Ultimate.

## New to the game? Try James (pistol)
- Basic attack: A reliable pistol with 17 damage and 0.85-second fire rate.
- Skill **Rapid Fire**: Doubles fire rate for 1.8 seconds.
- Ultimate **Power Shot**: Your next shot becomes a big, fast bullet that deals 66 damage.
- Tip: Keep the Ultimate ready and fire when you know you'll land it. Hold R and click to fire that shot right away.

## Pick by type
- In the codex, you can filter characters by type, like **Gun, Melee, Throwing, Explosive, Shotgun, Card**. Slaughterer and Cleaner are special characters that don't belong to any type.
- Guns: James, Agent, Robin Hood, Ninja, Soldier, Gambler, Wizard, Dimension Traveler (8)
- Melee: Jadai, Horemheb, Knight, Baseball Player, Boxer, Assassin, Dracula, Pirate, Samurai (9)
- Throwing: Hunter, Kurus (2)
- Explosive: Bomber, Heavy Gunner (2)
- Shotgun: Sheriff, Card: Magician, Special: Slaughterer, Cleaner

## Which character suits you?
- Easy to aim: Weapons that fly fast in a straight line, like the pistol (James), assault rifle (Soldier) and shuriken (Ninja).
- If you like fighting at range: Robin Hood (arcing shots), Gambler (long range), the vacuum (480 range), Wizard (piercing).
- If you like getting up close: Short-cooldown melee characters like Boxer, Assassin and Pirate are easy to pick up.
- If you love big single hits: Heavy Gunner (68), Bomber (52), Baseball Player (43).
- If you want to support your team: Wizard's Magic Circle gives allies an attack boost and 8 healing per second. It's especially solid in team modes.
- The busiest characters to play are Kurus, Dimension Traveler and Gambler. Give them a shot once you know the rules.

## Character ranks and exclusive skins
- Each character ranks up based on total kills with that character: Novice 0, Bronze 10, Silver 30, Gold 60, Platinum 100, Diamond 200, Obsidian 350, Master 550, Grandmaster 800 kills.
- Reaching Diamond automatically unlocks that character's first tier-exclusive skin, and reaching Grandmaster unlocks the second.
- Mastery level goes up separately. Details are on the Progression page.

## Codex and balance
- The character codex on the site lists each character's strong and weak matchups. These are measured from bot-vs-bot matches, so real games can differ.
- The Balance page on the site shows each character's win rate and the numbers changed in each patch. Since v240, every pair is measured with 4 games per map across all 23 maps, for 27,600 games total.

- Skill **Card Line**: Fires 5 cards in a straight line toward your aim direction (10 damage each).
- Ultimate **Escape Trick**: Teleport to the nearest opponent, fire cards 3 times in a row with no cooldown for 1 second, then return to where you were after 1 second.
- Hits needed to burn through 300 HP: 9 (when all 3 cards hit and the bonus damage lands)

- Ultimate **Flame Shield**: Places a shield in front of you that blocks up to 60 damage. It lasts 8 seconds, follows you, and always stays in front of the direction you're facing. It breaks after blocking 60. It can't block piercing attacks, but it halves their damage and loses that much durability.
- The most direct damage you can deal in one sustained burst is about 255 (7.5 seconds times 34 per second).
- Tip: Using the full 7.5 seconds leaves you defenseless while overheated. Fire in bursts to avoid overheating. You can't hit enemies behind platforms.
- Recent changes: In v229, flames were changed so they can't pass through platforms, and the max duration dropped from 10 seconds to 9 seconds (v229), 8 seconds (v236) and 7.5 seconds (v237). Flame Shield durability dropped from 75 to 60 (v237).

- Skill **Suction**: Pulls nearby enemies in and adds 1 stack.
- Ultimate **Dust Storm**: Blasts dust out of the vacuum, shoving opponents hard and dealing damage equal to your stacks times 10. Its range is half your basic attack's, and using it resets your stacks.

Collect gold (G) and soul stones (💜) to buy cosmetics, and earn rewards from missions, the Season Pass and achievements. Practice Mode and private rooms don't give any rewards.

## How to earn gold
- 1 kill: 10 gold and 1 soul stone. Killing a teammate gives nothing.
- 1 assist: 3 gold (no soul stone). You get an assist if you damaged an opponent within 10 seconds before they died.
- Finishing the tutorial: 100 gold (new accounts only).
- You get gold every time a character's mastery level goes up: level times 5 gold, and it stops increasing from Lv.20. Reaching Lv.10 gives a bonus 50 gold.
- Daily missions, weekly missions, the Season Pass, daily rewards, random boxes and achievements also give gold.
- A successful Boss Raid gives role bonuses (25–50 gold).
- Exchanging Hub Coin also gets you gold. See the Hub Coin Exchange page.
- Mastery XP is 10 per kill, 5 per assist, 5 for playing a match and 10 for a win. It doesn't build up in weaponless modes (Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek, Survival, Parkour).

## How to earn soul stones
- You get 1 for every kill.
- They also come from finishing weekly missions (5 each), Season Pass tier rewards and random boxes.
- Soul stones are only used to buy random boxes.

## Cosmetics shop
- Tabs: Skins, Tier Exclusive, Name Colors, Character Colors, Kill Effects, Profile Backgrounds, Profile Borders, Emotes, Victory Poses, Boxes
- Prices and details for each type are on the Cosmetics Shop Guide page.
- You can also gift cosmetics to friends. Logged-in friends can send each other cosmetics that are buyable with gold, and if your friend already owns it, they get its price in gold instead. You can include a short message (up to 40 characters).

- Cost 10 soul stones. Open them in the Boxes tab of the shop.
- Possible drops: 10, 20, 30 or 50 gold, 40 random character XP, 80 player XP, 5, 10 or 15 soul stones, or 1 skin worth 400 G or less
- The chance of a skin is 10%. You won't get skins you already own, and if there are no skins left to get, it turns into 50 gold.
- Skins from boxes are basic skins priced at 400 G or less. New skins and tier-exclusive skins don't drop.

## Daily rewards
- Once a day you get one gift: 30 gold (30%), 30 random character XP (25%), 60 player XP (25%) or 1 random box (20%).
- The date follows your device's date. If you set your device clock back, you can't claim it.

## Missions and Season Pass
- Details are on the Progression page. Each daily mission gives 30 gold, and each weekly mission gives 150 gold and 5 soul stones.

## Achievements
Completing an achievement gives you gold once. The in-game achievement list only shows names and keeps the conditions secret. Here are the conditions and rewards.

Each character has one. Use that character's Skill or Ultimate a set number of times in a single match to get 150–250 G. Skills have a 5-second cooldown and Ultimates 20 seconds, so Ultimate achievements need long matches.
- 250 G: Assassin Master of Stealth (Ultimate 10 times), Jadai Lightning Strikes the Same Place 9 More Times (Ultimate 10 times), Magician Escape Artist (Ultimate 10 times), Dracula I Am the Bat (Ultimate 5 times)

stickseum/growth.b:
:: Level cap = None
:: XP per kill = 36
:: Total XP for Lv.10 = 4,050
:: Daily missions = 3 (30 gold each)
:: Weekly missions = 3 (every Monday)
:: Season Pass = 20 tiers (300 XP each)

Here's everything that grows as you play. None of it builds up in Practice Mode or private rooms.

## Player level
- There's no level cap. You earn 36 XP per kill, 10 per assist, 10 for finishing a match, and another 36 for winning.
- Up to level 10, the curve keeps getting steeper. Total XP needed: Lv.2 is 50, Lv.3 is 200, Lv.4 is 450, Lv.5 is 800, Lv.6 is 1,250, Lv.7 is 1,800, Lv.8 is 2,450, Lv.9 is 3,200, Lv.10 is 4,050.
- After Lv.10, every level takes 950 XP. Lv.11 is 5,000, Lv.12 is 5,950, and so on.
- You also get XP from Capture the Flag captures (50 XP), finishing first in the MVP vote (50 XP), random boxes and daily rewards, and Season Pass rewards.
- There are achievements for reaching level 10 and level 25.

## Character mastery
- A separate level for each character. If you're holding that character when the match ends, it earns XP: 10 per kill, 5 per assist, 5 for playing the match, 10 for a win.
- It doesn't build up in modes without weapon picks (Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek, Survival, Parkour).
- Total XP needed: Lv.2 40, Lv.3 100, Lv.4 200, Lv.5 350, Lv.6 550, Lv.7 800, Lv.8 1,100, Lv.9 1,450, Lv.10 1,850.
- After Lv.10, XP per level starts at 450 and goes up by 50 each level, then stays at 950 from Lv.20. Lv.11 is 2,300, Lv.15 is 4,600, Lv.20 is 8,600.
- Every level-up gives gold: level times 5 gold, flat at 100 gold from Lv.20. Lv.10 gives a bonus 50 gold.
- At Lv.5, 10 and 20, that character's titles unlock (Adept, Expert, Legend).
- Lv.10 unlocks that character's profile background, and Lv.20 its profile border.
- Character XP from boxes and daily rewards goes to one random character.

## Character ranks (by kills)
- Based on total kills with that character: Novice 0, Bronze 10, Silver 30, Gold 60, Platinum 100, Diamond 200, Obsidian 350, Master 550, Grandmaster 800.
- Reaching Diamond and Grandmaster unlocks tier-exclusive skins.
- These go up separately from mastery level.

## Daily and weekly missions
- 3 new daily missions appear every day. Each one you finish gives 30 gold and 30 Season XP.
- 3 weekly missions change every Monday. Each one you finish gives 150 gold, 5 soul stones and 120 Season XP.
- When you finish a mission, you have to claim the reward yourself on the missions screen (📋).
- Daily mission pool: 3, 5 or 8 kills / 1 win / finish 2, 3 or 4 matches / 1,000 damage / 4 assists / 3 or 4 kills with gun characters / 3 or 4 kills with melee characters / a Domination, Team Battle or Deathmatch match. 3 of these are picked.
- Weekly mission pool: 25 or 40 kills / 4 or 6 wins / finish 12 or 18 matches / 4,000 or 6,000 damage / 10 or 15 assists / 3 Domination matches / 2 Capture the Flag matches / 2 Zombie Game matches / 15 kills with gun characters / 15 kills with melee characters.
- Gun characters are the ones the codex classifies as guns (James, Agent, Robin Hood, Ninja, Soldier, Gambler, Wizard, Dimension Traveler), and melee characters are Jadai, Horemheb, Knight, Baseball Player, Boxer, Assassin, Dracula, Pirate and Samurai.

## Season Pass
- A season is one calendar month. It follows your device's date, and when the month changes, your Season XP and claimed rewards reset.
- There are 20 tiers, and each tier takes 300 Season XP (6,000 to fill it all).
- You earn 20 Season XP for every match you finish, 20 more for winning, and 5 per kill (up to 15 kills per match). Mission rewards include Season XP too.
- When you reach a new tier, claim the reward yourself on the missions screen.
- Tier rewards:
- Tier 1: 50 gold, Tier 2: 3 soul stones, Tier 3: 1 random box, Tier 4: 80 gold, Tier 5: Starlight Burst kill effect
- Tier 6: 120 player XP, Tier 7: 5 soul stones, Tier 8: 100 gold, Tier 9: 1 random box, Tier 10: Season Veteran title
- Tier 11: 120 gold, Tier 12: 80 random character XP, Tier 13: 8 soul stones, Tier 14: 1 random box, Tier 15: Ice Shards kill effect
- Tier 16: 150 gold, Tier 17: 200 player XP, Tier 18: 10 soul stones, Tier 19: 2 random boxes, Tier 20: Season Master title

:: Username = 3–16 letters and numbers
:: Nickname = Up to 12 characters
:: Room code = 6 characters
:: Party = Up to 4 (including you)
:: Clan name = 2–12 characters
:: Invite expiry = 3 hours

Everything about playing with friends. Most of it requires logging in with a Frenchfries777 account.

## Account
- Log in or create an account from the Friends panel on the main screen. Usernames are 3–16 letters and numbers, and passwords are 6 or more characters.
- One Frenchfries777 account also logs you into Frenchfries777's other games (Crown Envoy, Beaconfall).
- Logging in with the same account carries over your friends, profile card and progress. Your profile card shows the games you've played and your Stickseum achievement progress.
- Nicknames can be up to 12 characters.

## Friends
- Search for friends by nickname and send a request. Once they accept, you're friends.
- Friend requests, clan invites and game invites expire automatically if not answered within 3 hours. After they expire, you can send them again.
- If a friend is in a match, an In Match tag shows next to them in your friend list and invites.
- After you connect and the intro finishes, any friend requests, clan invites and room invites you received are shown together.
- You can gift cosmetics from your friend list. If your friend is online they get it right away; otherwise they get it the next time they log in.
- You can find people you played with again under Recent Players on the records screen.

## Private rooms
1. In Private Play, set the mode and map (room settings) and hit Create Room.
2. Send the 6-character code to your friends. They enter it under Join with Code and hit Join.
3. The host hits Start. If you're short on players, you can add bots (Easy, Normal, Hard).
- Use the Invite Friends button in the room to send an invite to logged-in friends. When they accept, they join the room.
- Every mode is available. The host picks the map and can turn on Map Vote and Auto Team Balance.
- Private rooms give no rewards. If the host leaves mid-match, someone else takes over as host and the match continues.

## Spectating
- You can join a private room just to watch using the Spectate button on the Join with Code screen. Enter the 6-character code and hit Spectate.
- Spectating ends when the match ends or the connection to the host drops.
- You can also spectate after being eliminated. In Battle Royale, Battle Royale Duo and Tournament, choose Spectate on the defeat screen. While spectating, there's a Leave button in the top right.

## Parties
- You can group up with online friends in a party of up to 4 (including you). Whoever creates the party is the party leader.
- While in a party, you can only play party modes: Team Battle, Domination, Capture the Flag, Battle Royale Duo and Boss Raid. Battle Royale Duo only works with a 2-person party.
- Only the party leader picks the mode. When the leader starts matchmaking, party members follow into the same room on the same team.
- If the party leader leaves, the party ends. Party invites can only go to friends, and the invite notification stays up for 20 seconds.
- You can't play Ranked or daily modes while in a party.

## Clans
- The Clan screen only opens when you're logged in. It has three tabs: Find Clan, My Clan and Create Clan.
- When creating one, you set: a name (2–12 characters), a tag (2–4 characters, English letters, numbers or Korean; shown as [tag] before nicknames), an emblem (16 free ones), a color (8 options) and a description (up to 30 characters). Names and tags already in use aren't allowed.
- You can only be in one clan at a time. Join by searching for a name or tag in Find Clan, or by clicking an invite a clan member sent you. The list is sorted by clan score.
- The clan leader can write a clan notice (up to 40 characters). It pops up when clan members log in.
- There's clan chat (up to 100 characters per message).
- Clan members have clan tokens and can donate them to the clan vault in batches of 10 or 50. The clan leader uses vault tokens to unlock special emblems: Diamond 100, Galaxy 150, Trident 200, Dragon 300, Comet 300, Castle 500.
- Winning an online match (one with 2 or more real players) reports a win to your clan. Clan rankings are also on the site's Leaderboard page.
- **Clan Match**: Start one from the My Clan screen to create a Team Battle room only clan members can join. No bots.
- If the clan leader leaves, the clan disbands and all members are removed. Members can leave anytime (click once, then click again to confirm).

stickseum/hub-coin.b:
:: Exchange rate = 5 gold per coin
:: Daily login = 10 coins per day
:: Login streak = +20 bonus coins every 7 days
:: Gift limit = 100 per day
:: Undo exchange = Not possible
:: Added in = v238 (2026-10-16)

Hub Coin is the shared coin of the Frenchfries777 hub. You can turn coins you've collected on the hub into Stickseum gold. Added in v238 (2026-10-16).

## What's the rate?
- 1 coin is 5 Stickseum gold. Exchanging 10 coins gets you 50 gold.
- For comparison, 1 kill is 10 gold, so the 10 coins (50 gold) from a daily check-in equal 5 kills.

## How to get coins
- Log in to the Frenchfries777 hub once a day to get 10 Hub Coin. Days run on Korean time.
- Every 7 days in a row you check in, you get a bonus 20 coins. You can see it on the hub's check-in calendar.
- You can gift coins to friends on the hub: 1–100 per gift, up to 100 per day.

## How to exchange
1. Log in on the hub. It has to be the same Frenchfries777 account you use in Stickseum.
2. In the hub's Hub Coin Exchange window, choose Stickseum, enter how many coins to exchange and hit Exchange. The hub deducts the coins and holds the gold for you.
3. Log in to Stickseum with the same account and the held gold is collected automatically. A "Hub Coin Exchange: gold + amount" notification appears.

## When the gold arrives
- It's checked right after you log in.
- It's also checked when the game window becomes visible again (when you come back from another tab or click the window again), but only if 15 seconds have passed since the last check.
- It isn't checked while a match is in progress. You'll get it after the match ends and you leave.
- Gold you've received is never paid out twice. Even with two windows open, it only arrives once.

## What can you buy?
- A New Skin (2,000 G) is 400 coins. At 10 a day, that's 40 days.
- A 300 G basic skin is 60 coins, and a 500 G emote is 100 coins.
- Random boxes can only be bought with soul stones, not gold. Use gold for cosmetics in the shop instead.
- Exchanges can't be undone. Double-check the number of coins before you exchange.

## Good to know about Hub Coin
- Coins live in your hub wallet. In the game, they show up as gold, not coins.
- You have to exchange at least 1 coin at a time, and you can't exchange more than you have.
- Each game has its own rate, shown in the hub's exchange window. For Stickseum, it's 5 gold per coin.
- When you exchange on the hub, the hub records the gold and Stickseum picks it up, so it might not show up in Stickseum right after you exchange.

## If it doesn't arrive
- Make sure you're logged in to the hub and Stickseum with the same Frenchfries777 account.
- Check whether the hub's exchange window says there's gold still waiting. If so, go back to a non-match screen in Stickseum and try again.

stickseum/tips.b:
:: Natural regen = None (heal after 3 s still)
:: Skill cooldown = 5 s
:: Ultimate cooldown = 20 s
:: Teleport = Arrives after 1 s
:: Emote reuse = 1.2 s
:: Boss Raid = 3-min time limit

These tips are based on what we confirmed in the code and rules. They're not the only right answers, just a good direction to start in.

## General
- There's no natural regeneration. After a fight, hide and stay still for just 3 seconds to heal 5 every 0.5 seconds. Shooting is fine.
- Skills are 5 seconds and Ultimates 20 seconds, so using them beats saving them. That said, timing-sensitive ones like Barrier or Homing Missile should be used when they'll land.
- Teleport arrives 1 second after you use it. Even if your opponent moves in the meantime, you still go where you aimed, so it's better to use it ahead of time than in a panic.
- Hold Shift and press the Skill or Ultimate key to use it right away on the nearest opponent. Handy when things get hectic.
- Emotes can be used again after 1.2 seconds. Say hi casually.

## Deathmatch
- It's a 3-minute match, so kills are your score. You respawn after just 5 seconds, so feel free to play aggressively.
- In the last 30 seconds or so, go for nearby opponents. A tie means a shared win.

## Battle Royale & Duo
- No respawns, so managing HP is everything. Pick fewer fights and make time to stand still and heal.
- In Duo, your team is out only when both of you are down. Don't give up if one of you falls.

## Team Battle & Domination
- Teammates can't pick the same character. Try splitting up roles on your team (Wizard supports allies with Magic Circle).
- In Domination, holding the point gives 1 point per second. The goal is 100, so holding it nonstop ends the game in 100 seconds. Fight close to the point. You respawn 5 seconds after dying.
- The point is the floating platform closest to the center of the map.

## Duel & Ranked
- You pick a character again every round. You can't reuse characters, so have 3 different characters ready for 3 rounds.
- Look at what your opponent used in the first round and pick a counter for the next.
- You have 15 seconds to pick a character. Decide ahead of time.

## Zombie Game
- Zombies have 1.45x move speed and 900 HP. Humans should group up and cover each other.
- Characters that can keep their distance (long-range guns, bows) have the edge. Explosive and knockback weapons are less effective since zombies take no knockback.

## Bomb Pass
- Click a nearby player to pass. You have to pass within 20 seconds, so pick a direction as soon as you get the bomb.
- Close the gap with Dash to make sure the pass lands, and after passing, get away from whoever has the bomb.

## Hide and Seek
- Hiders should disguise themselves as platforms in spots the seeker is unlikely to check. The first 10 seconds, while the seeker's screen is covered, are key.
- You have 1 HP; if the seeker's first shot hits you, your platform disguise breaks and you can move. A second hit eliminates you.
- The seeker has to find everyone within 1 minute 30 seconds.

## Parkour
- No weapons, no Dash. Just focus on jump timing and items. Grabbing items along the way lets you shove nearby opponents.

## Survival
- You have 1 HP, so one hit and you're done. Use the 9 seconds before each disaster to find a safe spot.
- Each disaster is one random pick from lightning, tsunami, volcano, acid rain, flood, meteors, bombs or zombies, lasting 12 seconds. They get stronger as rounds go on.
- Survive five of them to win.

## Capture the Flag
- The flag carrier can't Teleport and moves a bit slower. Have a teammate escort them.
- Your flag has to be at your base for you to score. If your flag has been taken, get it back first.
- Scoring gives XP. You respawn at your base 5 seconds after dying.

## Boss Raid
- When a red circle flashes, jump. The ground slam does 22 damage.
- Minions spawn at 70%, 50% and 30% boss HP. Clearing minions can earn you the Cleanup bonus.
- Split the Damage Dealer, Tank, Cleanup and MVP roles so everyone gets a bonus. You only get them if the raid succeeds.
- The time limit is 3 minutes.

## Tournament
- You have to win 4 best-of-3 1v1 matches (first to 2) to win it all. You pick a character again every round. Unlike Duel, you can pick the same character again.
- In the final, the arena shrinks. Don't run; get in there.

## Daily modes
- In Protect the King, split roles between going for the enemy King and guarding your own. Non-Kings respawn after 5 seconds.
- In King of the Hill, your score only goes up when you're alone on the point. With two people it stops, so chase the other person off.
- In Weapon Relay, your character only changes when you get a kill. Don't give up when you're stuck on a weak character.
- In One Shot, everyone has 1 HP. Rapid-fire weapons hit most easily.
- In Paint War, covering lots of ground is how you score. Run around more than you fight.
- In Bounty Hunt, the leader (3+ points) gets a bounty. If you're the leader, hide; if not, go after the leader (worth 4 points).
- In Low-Gravity Brawl, knockback is strong and you fly far. High-knockback weapons like Home Run or the shotgun work great.

## Map tips
- Push opponents into the minecart (Underground Mine) or the freezing water (Frozen Lake) to damage them.
- The waves on Storm Pirate Ship alternate direction, so watch for the dark ripple before each wave arrives.
- On Dark Swamp, stay out of the big swamp in the center and cross on the stepping-stone platforms. Everyone inside the swamp slows down and sees less.

Common questions and what to check when something goes wrong.

## Getting started & installing
- How do I open the downloaded file? Just double-click it and it opens in your browser (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox). No installation or extra programs needed. You do need an internet connection.
- Why are old versions still around? They're kept in case you want to look at an older version. To play with friends, use the latest version.
- Does it work on phones? The site help recommends a computer since it's a keyboard-and-mouse game. Touch controls turn on automatically on touch devices, so you can give it a try. Turn your screen to landscape.
- The game name is different from before. It used to be called ArenaClash and StickmanRumble, and now it's Stickseum.

## Saving & accounts
- Where is my progress (gold, skins, level) saved? If you're not logged in, it's saved only in the browser you're using. If the site address changes or you open the game as a file, that's separate storage, so you start fresh.
- What happens when I log in? Log in with a Frenchfries777 account and your progress is also saved to your account, and logging in on another device loads or merges it. Your friends and profile carry over too.
- Will my records disappear if I switch accounts? If this browser has records from playing on another account, it loads the new account's progress and keeps the previous records stored separately in this browser.

## Playing with friends
- My friend can't join the room. Check that the code is right (6 characters, uppercase letters and numbers) and that you're on the same version. If everyone joins through Play Now on the site, you're all on the same latest version.
- Chat or skins don't show up for one person. That's because your versions differ. Use the same latest version.
- The host left. If a match is in progress, someone else takes over as host and the match continues. If the host doesn't respond for more than 8 seconds, it switches automatically too.
- My friend request disappeared. Friend requests, clan invites and game invites expire after 3 hours. Send it again.

## Rewards & progress
- My gold or XP isn't going up. Practice Mode and private rooms don't give XP, gold, soul stones, missions, achievements or mastery.
- My mastery isn't going up. Bomb Pass, Hide and Seek, Survival and Parkour don't involve picking a weapon, so mastery doesn't build up.
- I finished a mission but didn't get the reward. You have to claim it yourself on the missions screen (📋). Same goes for Season Pass tier rewards.
- I can't see achievement conditions. The in-game list only shows names and keeps the conditions secret. The conditions are on the Shop, Gold & Achievements page.
- How do I get tier-exclusive skins? They unlock automatically at 200 total kills (Diamond) and 800 kills (Grandmaster) with that character. They can't be bought in the shop.
- My Hub Coin exchange gold didn't arrive. See the "If it doesn't arrive" section on the Hub Coin Exchange page.

## Ranked
- My points aren't changing. Both players have to be logged in for it to count. Points also don't change after more than 3 matches with the same opponent within 24 hours.
- Will I face bots in Ranked? No. Ranked only matches logged-in players against each other.
- When does the season change? On the 1st of every month (Korean time), everyone restarts at 1000 points.

## Performance & display
- The game is slow. Try setting Graphics Effects to Low or Frame Limit to 30 FPS in Settings. Turn on Show FPS to see your current speed.
- The game looks frozen. When the game tab goes into the background, the browser slows it down. Keep the tab in front.
- There's no sound. Check that Sound Effects is turned on in Settings.
- I get touch controls on my iPad with a keyboard attached. Change Control Type to Computer in Settings.
- My controls are acting weird. Use Reset to Defaults under Key Bindings in Settings.

## Rules questions
- How long is Boss Raid? The time limit is 3 minutes.
- When does Deathmatch end? It ends after 3 minutes, and whoever has the most kills wins.
- When does the daily mode change? When your device's date changes.
- I can't pick the same character as my teammate. Duplicates aren't allowed within the same team.
